facts.statement: The genus Itasuchus was first described by Price in 1955.
facts.quote: authority: Price, 1955

facts.statement: Fossils of the type species Itasuchus jesuinoi were first found in the Serra da Galga Formation.
facts.quote: Fossils of the type species I. jesuinoi, first described in 1955 by Llewellyn Ivor Price, have been found from the Serra da Galga Formation

facts.statement: Later fossil finds support the presence of Itasuchus in the Presidente Prudente Formation.
facts.quote: though later finds also support its presence in the sediments of the Presidente Prudente Formation

facts.statement: Itasuchus had an elongated, flattened snout with interlocking teeth similar to modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: It possessed a somewhat elongated and flattened snout with interlocking teeth similar to what is seen in modern crocodilians

facts.statement: Itasuchus possessed thick osteoderm armor that may have been covered by a layer of leathery skin.
facts.quote: a thick osteoderm armor potentially covered by a thick layer of leathery skin

facts.statement: The family Itasuchidae was established in 2004 to include Itasuchus and Malawisuchus.
facts.quote: Itasuchus is the namesake of the family Itasuchidae, established in 2004 to accommodate both it and Malawisuchus

facts.statement: The clade Itasuchidae was redefined by Pinheiro and colleagues in 2018 to include other similar forms.
facts.quote: Itasuchidae did not see widespread use at first until the clade was redefined by Pinheiro and colleagues in 2018

facts.statement: It is frequently thought that Itasuchus and its relatives were close relatives of the Peirosauridae within the Notosuchia clade.
facts.quote: It is now frequently thought that regardless of the nomenclature, Itasuchus and its relatives were close kin to the Peirosauridae within the clade Notosuchia

facts.statement: Itasuchus lived in river systems during the late Campanian and early Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: Itasuchus inhabitet the meandering river systems of the Presidente Prudente and Serra da Galga Formation during the late Campanian and early Maastrichtian

facts.statement: The laterally flattened tail and keeled osteoderms of Itasuchus may have helped make the animal more hydrodynamic.
facts.quote: This is supported by the laterally flattened tail and keeled osteoderms, which may have been a factor in making the animal more hydrodynamic

facts.statement: Itasuchus was named by Llewellyn Ivor Price in 1955 based on fossils found near Peirópolis.
facts.quote: Itasuchus was named by Brazilian paleontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price in 1955 based on fossil material recovered near Peirópolis

facts.statement: The original description of Itasuchus was primarily based on cranial remains.
facts.quote: The description of the genus, which was published in the same study as that of Peirosaurus, was chiefly based on the cranial remains

facts.statement: By 2018, a second specimen, MUGEO 218-V, was referred to the genus Itasuchus at the genus level only.
facts.quote: By 2018 a second specimen, MUGEO 218-V, had also been referred to the genus Itasuchus, although only at a genus level

facts.statement: The name Itasuchus is derived from the Tupi word for 'stone' and the Greek word for 'crocodile'.
facts.quote: The name Itasuchus derives from the Tupi word "ita" for "stone" and "suchus", the Greek word for "crocodile"

facts.statement: The species name honors Jesuino Felicissimo Junior, who reported the first fossils found at the site.
facts.quote: The species name derives from Jesuino Felicissimo Junior, who is credited for having reported the first fossils from the site that yielded the remains of Itasuchus

facts.statement: It is debated whether Caririsuchus camposi should be classified as a species of Itasuchus, a proposal made by Buffetaut that was not widely accepted.
facts.quote: While maintaining the status of Caririsuchus as a distinct species, Buffetaut noted several similarities to Itasuchus, ultimately regarding Caririsuchus camposi a species of Itasuchus, creating the combination Itasuchus camposi

facts.statement: The skull of Itasuchus was estimated to be approximately 37 cm long, while the lower jaw could reach up to 43 cm in length.
facts.quote: Price estimated that the skull of Itasuchus was approximately 37 cm long, with a mandibular length of up to 43 cm.

facts.statement: The nostrils of Itasuchus opened forward and upward near the tip of the snout.
facts.quote: The nares open anterodorsally, meaning forward and upward, and were located close to the snout tip.

facts.statement: The quadratojugal bone in Itasuchus is small and does not help articulate the lower jaw.
facts.quote: The quadratojugal is described as small and does not participate in the articulation for the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Each premaxilla of Itasuchus likely contained five teeth, with the third tooth being the largest.
facts.quote: Based on the tentatively referred rostrum each premaxilla of Itasuchus likely housed five teeth, the third of which being the largest.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Itasuchus likely contained 18 teeth, though two are missing from the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: The lower jaw is better preserved and likely contained 18 teeth, which includes two that are missing in the holotype.

facts.statement: Itasuchus exhibits a crocodyloid occlusal pattern where teeth interlock like in modern crocodiles, unlike the pronounced overbite of alligators.
facts.quote: Overall Itasuchus displays what is generally referred to as a crocodyloid occlusal pattern, meaning that the teeth interlock similar to what is seen in modern crocodiles and unlike in alligators, which have a pronounced overbite.

facts.statement: The lower jaw teeth of Itasuchus feature a distinct pair of contiguous tooth sockets that stand out among the others.
facts.quote: The dentary toothrow of Itasuchus also features a distinct pair of couplets that stand out among the remainder of the teeth for their position.

facts.statement: The surface of Itasuchus osteoderms featured small deep pits that sometimes formed canals radiating from a central keel.
facts.quote: The surface is ornamented by small but deep pits, sometimes joining into canals that radiate outward from a keel that runs down each individual plate lengthwise with an outward curvature.

facts.statement: The anterior surface of each Itasuchus osteoderm was bevelled to allow overlapping with the plate behind it.
facts.quote: The anterior surface of each single osteoderm is bevelled, allowing each osteoderm to overlap the one behind it.

facts.statement: Histology shows that Sharpey's fibers in Itasuchus osteoderms were inserted perpendicular to the outer bone surface.
facts.quote: Histology of the osteoderms of Itasuchus has further revealed that the sharpey's fibres, which anchor the bony plates to the underlying tissue, were inserted into the external cortex of the bone perpendicular to the outer surface.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Itasuchus osteoderms may have been deeply embedded under a layer of leathery skin in life.
facts.quote: Based on this Sena and colleagues have suggested that in life the osteoderms of Itasuchus may have been more deeply embedded than they are in modern crocodilians and could have been covered by a layer of leathery skin.

facts.statement: Among related species, Itasuchus was likely the heaviest due to its thicker armor.
facts.quote: though the they also note that among these three Itasuchus was likely the heaviest on account of its thicker armor, especially if it was similarly well armored as the closely related Caririsuchus.

facts.statement: Woodward and colleagues estimated the body weight of Itasuchus to be between 132.84 and 194.91 kg in 2025.
facts.quote: A precise estimate was provided by Woodward and colleagues in 2025. Based on the length of the femur they calculate a body weight ranging between 132.84-194.91 kg.

facts.statement: Itasuchus is interpreted as a semi-aquatic animal.
facts.quote: Like other closely related species Itasuchus has been interpreted as a semi-aquatic animal.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Itasuchus are cited as evidence for its semi-aquatic lifestyle.
facts.quote: the osteoderms have also been cited as evidence for such a lifestyle.

facts.statement: Marinho and colleagues argue that the keels on Itasuchus osteoderms made the animal hydrodynamic and stable when submerged.
facts.quote: Marinho and colleagues have argued that the pronounced keels on the dorsal osteoderms of Itasuchus made the animal more hydrodynamic and stabilized it when it was fully submerged.

facts.statement: The laterally flattened tail and shifted keels of Itasuchus effectively created a paddle.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the team describes the tail of Itasuchus as laterally flattened, which together with the shifted keels in the laterodorsal tail osteoderms effectively creates a paddle.

facts.statement: Marinho and colleagues hypothesize that Itasuchus had difficulty moving on land due to its heavy armor.
facts.quote: Marinho and colleagues also hypothesize that compared to the more terrestrial peirosaurids and even modern crocodilians, animals like Itasuchus would have had a harder time moving on land on account of their heavier, more restrictive osteoderm armor.

facts.statement: The large surface area of Itasuchus osteoderms likely helped it absorb heat efficiently and become active quickly.
facts.quote: In turn the large surface area of Itasuchus osteoderms would have been an advantage when it came to raising the animals body temperature, allowing it to absorb heat more efficiently and helping it become active quicker than the terrestrial peirosaurids.

facts.statement: A 2023 analysis placed Itasuchus close to the brevirostrine peirosaurid Antaeusuchus.
facts.quote: In a 2023 morphospace analysis itasuchids as a whole were recovered to represent an intermediate between long-snouted and brevirostrine forms, with Itasuchus in particular having been found close to the brevirostrine peirosaurid Antaeusuchus.

facts.statement: In 2004, Carvalho and colleagues coined the family Itasuchidae to unite Itasuchus with Malawisuchus.
facts.quote: In 2004 Carvalho and colleagues coined the family Itasuchidae, initially meant to unite Itasuchus with the African crocodyliform Malawisuchus as the sister group to Peirosauridae within Notosuchia.

facts.statement: The clade name Itasuchidae was revived in 2018 by Pinheiro and colleagues.
facts.quote: the clade name was eventually revived in 2018 by Pinheiro and colleagues in their redescription of "Goniopholis" paulistanus as Roxochampsa.

facts.statement: The placement of Itasuchus in Trematochampsidae is debated due to potential issues with the holotype of Trematochampsa.
facts.quote: However this hypothesis too came into question due to the fact that the holotype of Trematochampsa may have been chimeric and the group had become a wastebasket of various unrelated animals.

facts.statement: The type species Itasuchus jesuinoi was described by Llewellyn Ivor Price in 1955 from fossils found in the Maastrichtian-aged Marília Formation in Uberaba, Brazil.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de la especie tipo I. jesuinoi, descritos originalmente en 1955 por Llewellyn Ivor Price, han sido hallados en la Formación Marília (edad del Maastrichtiense) en Uberaba, Brasil.

facts.statement: Itasuchus is known from a skull 370 mm long, suggesting a total body length of about 3 meters.
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir de un cráneo de 370 milímetros de largo, lo que sugiere una longitud total de cerca de 3 metros.

facts.statement: The environment where Itasuchus lived likely had an arid to semi-arid climate that experienced wetter periods.
